purpose: Complete the four items the canonical data classification left open: per-class retention, database-level encryption requirements, integrity-verification requirements, and an outbound telemetry rule for C2_BUSINESS_CONFIDENTIAL.
requiredInvariants: Documented requirement and proven enforcement are recorded separately for every class; neither is inferred from the other.
A retention value grounded in a named statute is labelled a proposed default pending confirmation, never a certified legal conclusion.
Every enforcement claim that names a file is checked by a test against that file's real content.
Completing the policy document may close V14.1.2 (documentation completeness); it must not by itself close any enforcement-focused requirement.
The C2 outbound rule is bound in code (OUTBOUND_REDACTED_CLASSES), not only stated in the document.
No security control is weakened; Semgrep, the pinning ratchet and every other gate stay at full strength.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation.
acceptance: Every class carries a retention, databaseEncryption and integrityVerification entry with a requirement and an enforcement statement.
The two prohibited classes are not-applicable across all three new dimensions.
C2's outbound redaction is proven by a Sentry-scrub test, not only by a schema flag.

Every cited enforcement fact (TTL constants, AES-256-GCM usage, the INN VarChar gap, the evidence-pack hash chain, contract-version immutability, the auth-mail retention job) is verified against the real file by test.
Three mutations were verified to turn the suite red: the C2 code binding removed (a compile-time failure), an enforcement citation gone stale, and a class silently losing its retention entry.
V14.2.7 stays FAIL, with its note updated to say the classification gap it named is closed and the enforcement gap is what remains.
The evidence gate rejects 0 decisions; finalPass stays false.
